title: CT fat-feature model predicts events within a deliberately enriched cohort
summary: DeepFat-assisted segmentation and a 15-feature elastic-net Cox model yielded a test C-index of 0.69 in 80 held-out patients from a 400-person, event-enriched cohort. Test-set risk reclassification was not statistically established. The result was already present in the January 2024 preprint; it is not evidence of general-population risk calibration or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: DeepFat deep-learning segmentation; elastic-net Cox model

source_review.scope: Actual relevant original clinical/computational Methods and Results read;111 original v1 and later journal checked separately; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A previously developed learned segmenter provides manually checked epicardial-fat masks; selected handcrafted spatial/intensity features enter a fitted regularized survival model. AI credit concerns measurement and model fitting, not a new fat-inflammation mechanism.
evidence.tested: The original v1 Methods and Results use 400 archived CT records, with 56% event prevalence and a random 320/80 development/test split. Feature selection is described as training-only. The v1 reports the same 0.69 test C-index as the later journal version.
evidence.unknown: The cohort was deliberately enriched by event/calcium-score groups, so natural prevalence, absolute risk and transportability are not established. DeepFat masks were manually corrected. The test reclassification statistic had a confidence interval crossing zero and p=0.463 despite a favorable narrative; no significant incremental reclassification claim is adopted. The composite includes revascularization and all-cause death. Later journal Methods/Results were separately read; they are not treated as a new discovery or silently backdated to v1.
